text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Wednesday.

GERMANY - Bunds and futures recovered in late trade to post gains ahead of a long holiday weekend but traders said concerns about the future of European monetary union still weighed on the market. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 100.96, up 0.20 from Tuesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts steadied off the day's lows after tracking Bunds lower for much of the session and ended just 2/32 lower on the day. Rumours that Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer had resigned or planned to resign unsettled markets until the Bundesbank said the rumours had absolutely no basis in fact. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 112-17/32, up 05/32 from Tuesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - Bond futures finished MATIF trading lower amid market talk of private opinion polls showing the left well placed ahead of Sunday's election runoff and weakness in the German bond market. The June bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 128.16, down 0.28 from Tuesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Bonds and futures ended weaker as a wave of selling hit European high-yielders and the lira. Traders said the impetus came from abroad and reflected nervousness over EMU with market rumours abounding. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 129.17, down 0.65 from Tuesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasury securities started on a weak footing, dragged down after European bonds dipped on French election worries. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 109-02/32, up 11/32 from Tuesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 7.0 percent.

JAPAN - The key June 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract ended sharply lower due to new ratings by Standard & Poor's of second-tier life insurers and a sharp rise in interest rate swap (IRS) rates. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 122.51, down 0.74 from Tuesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The primary market saw more mainstream activity following a focus on the emerging market sector on Tuesday. Associates Corp raised $500 million over 10-years while British Columbia also raised $500 million over 10-years. The EIB set a 250 million stg December 2006 fungible bond. Cerinvest set a 60 million euro December 2002 bond.
